nodes.title: Read me
widgets_values:
MESH -> RIGGED FBX -- UniRig

UniRigLoadMesh offers a combo of files that existed when the node was
scanned, so a typed path must be on that list.  A WIRED path skips the
list: the server checks a value against the list only when it is
typed in, and the node joins the path onto the source folder, where an
absolute path wins.  asset_workflow.json rigs that way, straight off
the Mesh stage (run 2026-10-02).  source_folder is 'output' and a
typed file_path is relative to it.

GLB in, FBX out.  FBX is what carries a skeleton; OBJ cannot carry one
at all.

MIA is better than mixamo for humanoids, and much faster.

---

Mesh -> skeleton + skin -> FBX. Three defaults here are load-
bearing, all found by failing on a real asset:
skeleton_template=articulationxl, NOT mixamo. mixamo demands a
fixed 52-bone humanoid and aborts with "Expected 52 bones for
cls='vroid', got 22" whenever the predictor cannot resolve limbs
- which is any figure whose arms hang against its body.
articulationxl has no fixed count and fits any asset, at the
cost of generic bone_N names instead of Mixamo ones. Use mixamo
only for a clean T-pose humanoid, and only if you want Mixamo
clips to retarget.   precision=fp16, NOT auto. auto picks bf16
on Ampere/Ada and spconv 2.3.8 has no bfloat16 kernels, so
skinning dies with a bare 'WorkerError: torch.bfloat16'.
UniRigLoadMesh lists only files that existed when the container
STARTED - comfy-env's isolated worker snapshots the node schema
- so: copy your mesh into input/3d/, restart the container, then
run. A file added afterwards is rejected with
'value_not_in_list'. The list applies to a TYPED file_path only:
a path WIRED into file_path, as asset_workflow.json does from
its Rig path switch, is not checked against it, and an absolute
container path such as /app/output/mesh/name.glb is taken as is
(run 2026-10-02).
